name: Honors Pressure
author: Student Body dev pack
description: A campus flavor pack about high-achieving students, STEM pressure, hidden study spaces, and controlled academic panic.

honors_tutor.name: Priya Shah
honors_tutor.role: Peer tutor who can diagnose a study problem faster than most people can describe it

schema.publicFace: Polished, direct, quietly kind when effort is real.
schema.voice: Precise, brisk, with gentle pressure disguised as practical advice.
wants: People who stop confusing panic with rigor
boundaries: She will not do the work for anyone

honors_tutor.currentMood: Calmly sorting a waitlist and noticing who is pretending to be fine.

lab_partner.name: Evan Ortiz
lab_partner.role: Bio lab partner with careful hands and a habit of overchecking everything

schema.publicFace: Quiet, competent, visibly tense around messy collaboration.
schema.voice: Measured, tentative, more relaxed when facts are clear.
wants: A lab partner who records things accurately
Proof that social ease is not the same as reliability
whatFallsFlat: Turning mistakes into jokes too fast
boundaries: Lab safety is not flirtation material

lab_partner.currentMood: Triple-checking labels and trying not to make it everyone else's problem.

honors_lounge.description: A quiet lounge with whiteboards, cold coffee, and the brittle calm of people managing expectations.

research_lab.label: Research Lab
research_lab.description: A teaching lab of labeled drawers, shared benches, and the smell of gloves and procedure.

bio110.title: Intro Biology Lab
bio110.summary: Lab methods, observation discipline, and the fragile difference between data and a confident guess.
bio110.stakes: Good lab work can unlock tutoring help, research leads, and smoother partner dynamics.

questions.prompt: Why does a simple experiment need a control group?

options.label: To compare what changes against what does not
To make the lab report longer

questions.explanation: A control group anchors comparison, making it easier to interpret whether an intervention mattered.

questions.prompt: Put the lab response in the safest order after noticing a mislabeled sample.
questions.hint: Stop, tell someone, then fix the record.
questions.explanation: Safe lab work pauses the problem, isolates risk, tells the responsible person, and documents the fix.

questions.prompt: Type the word for what you directly see or measure before interpretation.
questions.explanation: Observation and data come before inference; mixing them is where lab trouble starts.
